# Data

## Data sources

ESC HF III

## Inclusion/exclusion criteria

```{r}
#| label: tbl-flow
#| tbl-cap: Information for flowchart
#| tbl-pos: "H"

default_kable(flow) %>%
  add_indent(6)
```

First patient in: `r min(escdata$BASEDT)` and last patient in: `r max(escdata$BASEDT)` 
from approximately `r escdata %>% distinct(CentreId) %>% count() %>% pull(n)` 
enrolling centers in `r escdata %>% distinct(COUNTRY) %>% count() %>% pull(n)` countries. 

## Definitions

EF is defined at admission, and if missing, during hospitalization and thirdly last known EF. 

# Statistical analysis 

## General

All analyses were performed using `r sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string` [@r]. 
The level of significance is set to 5%, two-sided. No adjustment for multiple 
comparisons were made and therefore the results should be viewed with care.

## Missing data

Missing data was imputed with multiple imputation (n = 20) using mice [@mice] 
and Rubin’s rules was used for combining estimates and standard errors across imputed data sets. 
Variables included in the model are indicated in @tbl-base. The outcomes were not imputed and the imputation was only used for the adjusted models for the outcomes. 

## Baseline characteristics

Categorical variables are presented with n and percentage and tested for 
differences with the chi-square test. 
Continuous variables are presented with median [first quartile-third quartile] and tested for 
differences with the Kruskal-Wallis test. 

## Descriptive presentations

Selected variables were presented descriptively with bar plots, box plots, violin plots and scatter plots with loess curves together with Kendall's tau correlation coefficient as appropriate.  

## Association between bilirubin and outcomes

Logistic regression models are used to model in-hospital death. 

Cox proportional hazards regression are used to model the time to death at approximately 1 year follow-up for patients discharged alive and available data. 

Negative binomial regression are used to model the composite outcome of number of heart failure hospitalisations and cv deaths at approximately 1 year follow-up for patients discharged alive and available data where the log of follow-up time was included as an offset in the model.  

The crude association between bilirubin and outcomes were presented graphically where bilirubin was modelled using a natural cubic spline with 3 knots placed at the quantiles and the reference set to 1.2. 

The adjusted association between bilirubin as a categorical variable and outcomes were performed where adjustment was performed for variables indicated in @tbl-base, where the continuous variables where modeled using natural cubic splines with 3 knots placed at the quantiles, and presented in Forest plots.  

In order to see if the results were consistent across subgroups an interaction effect between bilirubin and EF, sex and age respectively was included in the adjusted models. 

The 1.2 cut-off for bilirubin was pre-specified and based on previous studies. However, we also explored the optimal cut-off for bilirubin using Youden's J statistic (Sensitivity + Specificity - 1) for the outcomes in-hospital death and death at approximately 1 year follow-up. 

### Assumptions

In the logistic regression multicollinearity was investigated using the Variance Inflation Factor and outliers were inspected using Cook's distance, both without cause for action. 

In the cox regression model the proportional hazards assumption was investigated using the scaled Schoenfeld 
residuals and possible outliers were visually inspected by plotting the dfbetas without cause for action. 

\clearpage

# Results

```{r}
med <- escdata %>%
  summarise(
    med = fn(median(DMAGE, na.rm = T), dig = 0),
    q1 = fn(quantile(DMAGE, na.rm = T, probs = 0.25), dig = 0),
    q3 = fn(quantile(DMAGE, na.rm = T, probs = 0.75), dig = 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(out = paste0(med, " (", q1, "-", q3, ")")) %>%
  pull(out)

medbili <- escdata %>%
  summarise(
    med = fn(median(Bili_mgdL, na.rm = T), dig = 1),
    min = fn(min(Bili_mgdL, na.rm = T), dig = 1),
    max = fn(max(Bili_mgdL, na.rm = T), dig = 1),
    q1 = fn(quantile(Bili_mgdL, na.rm = T, probs = 0.25), dig = 1),
    q3 = fn(quantile(Bili_mgdL, na.rm = T, probs = 0.75), dig = 1)
  ) %>%
  mutate(out = paste0(med, " (", min, ", ", q1, "-", q3, ", ", max, ")")) %>%
  pull(out)

percfem <- escdata %>%
  count(DMSEX) %>%
  mutate(perc = fn(n / sum(n) * 100, 0)) %>%
  filter(DMSEX == "Female") %>%
  pull(perc)
```

The median (q1-q3) age is `r med` and `r percfem`% females. The median (min, q1-q3, max) bilirubin is `r medbili`.
